## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Dasamanaya Vippayuttenavippayuttapadaniddesa* constitutes the tenth method (*naya*) of the *Dhātukathā*, the third book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The title designates the exposition (*niddesa*) of states dissociated (*vippayutta*) from what is itself dissociated (*vippayuttena*). SuttaCentral records one translation in one language for this text [SuttaCentral].

DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse, with 6,685 matching passages across 31 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The closest internal alignments occur with other sections of the *Dhātukathā*, especially the ninth chapter (*Navamanaya Sampayuttenasampayuttapadaniddesa*, Dt 2.9), the fourteenth chapter (*Cuddasamanaya Vippayuttenasaṅgahitāsaṅgahitapadaniddesa*, Dt 2.14), and the sixth chapter (*Chaṭṭhanaya Sampayogavippayogapadaniddesa*, Dt 2.6), as well as Dt 2.7, Dt 2.13, and Dt 2.5 [DharmaNexus]. Outside the *Dhātukathā*, substantial shared material appears in the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi*, the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* (*Dukanikkhepa*, Ds 2.3.2), and later subcommentarial literature such as the *Pañcapakaraṇa-anuṭīkā* and the *Visuddhimagga-mahāṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Across languages, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages with Tibetan translations of northern scholastic texts, including Sthiramati's *Abhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā* (D4054), Vasubandhu's *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (D4090), and the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* (D0009) [DharmaNexus].
